record.name: Saša Todić
record.title: Professor Emeritus
record.bio: Saša Todić received his undergraduate and master's degrees in economics from the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Economics in Subotica, and completed his doctorate at the University of Belgrade Faculty of Economics in 1993, with a dissertation on credit risk pricing in transitional banking systems. He joined the Faculty of Economics in Subotica as an assistant in 1990 and rose to full professor before retiring and receiving emeritus status in 2019. His research focused on the resolution of non-performing loans in thin secondary debt markets, covering servicer incentive structures, collateral liquidation procedures, and recovery rate determinants across Central and South-Eastern European banking systems. He taught courses in commercial banking, credit analysis, and financial intermediation for three decades.
record.industry_experience: Todić served as an expert advisor to the National Bank of Serbia's Financial Stability Department on two occasions (2004–2005 and 2012–2013), providing technical input on NPL classification standards and servicer licensing criteria. He has also acted as an independent expert witness in commercial court proceedings involving disputed loan recovery calculations.
record.notes: Emeritus status; not available for project leadership, teaching duties, or regular institutional commitments. Available for time-limited consulting engagements, particularly on NPL valuation methodology, servicer contract design, and regulatory gap analysis for secondary debt market development. Prefers written briefs over sustained project involvement. Co-authorship requests from former colleagues are considered case by case.
